title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 1 Cor. 15 in Adam all die: each his own death; rise in Christ really, not by imputed resurrection
pass_a_gloss: Against 1 Cor. 15 'in Adam all die': Placeus says the verse overturns the other side. Paul does not mean all die by Adam's one singular death imputed to everyone, but each by his own proper death. Rising in Christ matches that—real resurrection each receives in himself, not imputation of Christ's rising.
pass_b_english: You also object a like phrase in a like matter from the same Apostle: in Adam all die. But that overturns your view. For he does not mean that all die in Adam by that very singular death by which Adam died, as if it were imputed to all, but each by his own proper death. So we are made alive, or rise, in Christ—not by imputation of Christ's resurrection, but by a real resurrection which each receives in himself.
source_text: Objicis etiam similem phrasim in re simili eiusdem Apostoli: in Adam omnes moriuntur. Sed ea tuam sententiam evertit. Non vult enim omnes mori in Adamo illa ipsa singulari morte, qua mortuus est Adamus, quae scilicet omnibus imputetur, sed sua quisque propria morte. Sic vivificamur, seu resurgimus in Christo; non per imputationem resurrectionis Christi, sed reali, & quam quisque in se suscipit, resurrectione.
